title: Temporary sovereign routing - operator guide and patchwork runbook
body:
Purpose:
This is an operator-oriented guide for short-lived sovereign routing / "patchwork" scenarios where we must temporarily route a subset of tenant traffic to a local region or partner cluster while long-term pinning is negotiated or capacity is stood up.

Audience:
- On-call operators and SREs
- Solutions engineers standing up quick temporary routes for enterprise trials
- Sales/success engineers coordinating with customers and legal

High-level constraints / framing (fast):
- Temporary routes must preserve tenant data residency assertions for the duration (evidence capture required).
- Goal: <72h live patch for most customers; longer if contract/grace window.
- No permanent changes to tenant canonical pin in control plane unless explicit change ticket is approved.
- Prefer proxying with redaction & evidence logging vs copying data where possible.
- Work should be reversible within operator window (clear exit path).

Quick decision matrix (operator checklist):
1) Customer request has legal approval? -> If yes, proceed. If no, escalate to product-legal.
2) Is local compute available (partner/local cluster)? -> If yes, prepare route. If no, initiate emergency deploy (see infra tasks below).
3) Traffic volume estimate low (<2 RPS per tenant) -> Use lightweight proxy route. High -> Need capacity/queueing approach.

Runbook steps (step-by-step):
1) Create a temporary routing ticket: PD-XXXX (use template: temporary-routing-runbook). Link to customer contract id + legal waiver.
2) Preflight telemetry snapshot: take region pin baseline (region_claimed, last_pin_change, request_count_24h). Attach to ticket.
3) Stand up ephemeral route:
   - Option A: Edge proxy rule (fastest): configure edge-rule in routing-service to rewrite tenant route to partner endpoint with header X-Temp-Pin and set TTL. TTL defaults to 72h.
   - Option B: GRE tunnel/proxy for high-volume: create ephemeral tunnel to local cluster using documented ssh-tunnel process. Use flow-control throttles.
   - Option C: Application-level redirect (only when both sides run compatible runtime): deploy route-shim sidecar on inbound gateway that forwards requests and streams tokens.
4) Add redaction filter: ensure PII fields marked by tag set 'sov-redact-v1' are scrubbed in any logs forwarding.
5) Evidence capture: enable evidence mode for the tenant for the route lifetime. Evidence mode must include request hash, timestamp, route decision, and endpoint id. Store evidence in audit bucket labeled with ticket id.
6) Smoke test with synthetic requests: use test account (not real customer) to validate success criteria: latency < 350ms median to partner, no token leakage in logs, KV-cache warm-up observed.
7) Invite customer success and legal to the ticket for live verification.
8) Monitor for 2x SLA period, then change ticket to 'observed-stable' before handing off back to product if longer run needed.

Operator knobs and commands (cheat sheet):
- routing-service CLI: rds route create --tenant <TENANT_ID> --target https://ephemeral.partner/ingest --ttl 72h --meta "temp_pin=partner-us-east"
- set evidence: rds evidence enable --tenant <TENANT_ID> --bucket audits/temp-pin-PD-XXXX --retention 90d
- redact filters: obsctl redact apply --set sov-redact-v1 --scope tenant:<TENANT_ID>
- rollback: rds route remove --tenant <TENANT_ID> --force; rds evidence disable --tenant <TENANT_ID>

Telemetry & signals (what to watch):
- route_select_rate: hits per minute for the temporary route (target stable < traffic estimate + 10%).
- cross_region_latency_p50/p95/p99 to partner endpoint.
- cache_miss_ratio for KV lookups (high miss indicates cold-start cost).
- audit-log-size growth for evidence bucket (must not exceed request).
- error rates: 5xx and 499s (client timeouts) -- threshold 0.5% sustained.
- privacy alerts: any filtered field showing raw PII in logs -> immediate rollback.

Failure modes & mitigations:
- Partner endpoint degradation: auto-fallback to hosted-unpinned route after 30s sustained p95 > 2s. Raise ticket to PD ops.
- Evidence bucket write failure: disable route immediately, set incident classification: residency-evidence-failure. Notify legal.
- Unexpected data residency claim drift: freeze route, capture snapshot, call product+legal, do not proceed until cleared.

Operator notes (practical lessons):
- Avoid changing canonical tenant pin during temporary exercises — causes drift in billing & audit.
- Use TTL markers on routes so stale temp-routes expire automatically if operator forgets to remove.
- Keep the evidence bucket name consistent pattern: audits/temp-pin-PD-<ticket>. Makes audits easier.
- For multi-tenant partner rollouts, stagger by customer by 5–10 minutes to avoid partner capacity spikes.

Testing matrix (minimal tests to run before going live):
- Functional: end-to-end request completes and returns with expected output.
- Telemetry: metrics emitted to obs platform within 60s.
- Security: redaction applied, no sensitive payload in logs.
- Legal: evidence bundle contains required fields (request hash, timestamps, route decision).

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Should we standardize a smaller TTL (24h) for trial customers? Tradeoff: operator churn vs safety. (PENDING: product/legal to advise)
- Automation: build a template in routing-service for ephemeral-pin so operators click-and-run. (Owner: Evan Park)
- Cost accounting: how to tag temporary routes for billing reconciliation? (Finance + Billing)

Customer communication snippets (when asked by sales/cs):
- "We're enabling a short-lived local routing path while we finalize residency contract details; no data is copied permanently and we capture audit evidence for the entire period."
- "This is a reversible change and will automatically expire if not extended."

Quick rollback checklist (when things go wrong):
1) Flip route TTL to 0: rds route remove --tenant <TENANT_ID>
2) Disable evidence capture to avoid partial writes: rds evidence disable --tenant <TENANT_ID>
3) Run diagnostic bundle and attach to ticket: obsctl diag collect --tenant <TENANT_ID> --since 1h --out /tmp/pd-xxxx-bundle.tgz
4) Notify legal + CS with incident classification and evidence snapshot link.

Notes to self / informal:
- This doc intentionally rough — meant to be a living operator cheat sheet.
- Save a copy to confluence when we converge on final automation template.
- Revisit redaction tags naming; current 'sov-redact-v1' likely to be versioned.

Appendix: Example evidence record (flat CSV row format expected in audit bucket):
- ticket_id,tenant_id,request_id,request_hash,route_target,route_time_iso,operator,notes

Links:
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/temporary-routing-runbook
- Playbook repo: git+ssh://git.redwood.ai/infraplaybooks/ephemeral-routing.git
- Related ticket: JIRA PD-1427

End.
